items.title: Honeycomb-Surfels: Compact Hexagonal Primitives for Efficient Scene Rendering and Reconstruction
items.summary: Hexels are planar hexagonal primitives with first-order color fields that enable efficient 3D scene rendering and reconstruction.
items.whyItMatters: They reduce memory and compute costs, making advanced view synthesis feasible on limited hardware.

items.title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
items.summary: ThinkWorld proposes using human videos to improve VLA models, balancing large-scale data with action grounding for better robotic manipulation.
items.whyItMatters: It could enable robots to learn more diverse tasks from everyday videos.

items.title: When Should We Intervene at Test Time?
items.summary: The article examines when to apply test‑time adaptation, noting that interventions like updating normalization can help or hurt depending on batch composition.
items.whyItMatters: Tech‑savvy readers need to know how to balance adaptation benefits against potential performance drops in dynamic deployments.

items.title: Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness
items.summary: Heads of Security uses learned attention gates to separate instruction and data, preventing prompt injection in large language models.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a lightweight, model-agnostic defense improving safety for high‑scale AI deployments.

items.title: Attention as Lattice Gauge Theory: Relations Interact Only Through Wilson Loops
items.summary: The article explains how relational composition can be modeled as a lattice gauge theory, using Wilson loops to verify consistency when entities have independent coordinate frames.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a novel, mathematically rigorous way to ensure data integrity in complex relational systems.

items.title: KPPax: preprocess differentiable kinetic ODE for machine learning in atmospheric chemistry
items.summary: KPPax converts Kinetic PreProcessor mechanisms into differentiable, JIT‑compiled JAX code for machine‑learning use.
items.whyItMatters: It enables gradient‑based learning on atmospheric chemistry models, improving integration with modern ML frameworks.

items.title: Pushing Dexterity and Safety for In-Hand Object Pose Reaching That Works Remarkably Well
items.summary: The paper presents a method for robots to reach specific object poses inside their grasp, improving dexterity and safety.
items.whyItMatters: It advances complex in-hand manipulation, crucial for advanced robotic applications like assembly and service tasks.

items.title: GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents
items.summary: GEPA-Curator enhances self‑improving agents by curating learning from diverse failure sources beyond failed rollouts, improving prompt quality and agent performance.
items.whyItMatters: It helps tech‑savvy readers build more robust, adaptable AI agents in complex environments.

items.title: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
items.summary: The article explores whether large language models can autonomously discover new physical laws by detecting unexpected phenomena and conducting experiments.
items.whyItMatters: It tests AI’s potential for scientific innovation and autonomous hypothesis generation.

items.title: Scaling Laws for Tool-Use Agents via Controllable Environment Synthesis
items.summary: The paper studies how synthetic environment diversity impacts training of LLM tool‑use agents for complex tasks, introducing the SynthAPI pipeline to control tool, task, and environment variation.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a scalable method to improve agent performance, crucial for deploying reliable AI in real‑world multi‑step workflows.

items.title: MuonGS: Pretraining LLMs with Relaxed Weight-Norm Control
items.summary: MuonGS studies how relaxed weight-norm control during LLM pretraining affects optimizer behavior and training dynamics.
items.whyItMatters: Understanding norm control can guide better regularization for more efficient, stable language model training.

items.title: Multi-State Linear Attention with Generalized Second-Order Routing
items.summary: The article introduces Multi-State Linear Attention, a method that reduces self-attention’s quadratic cost by segmenting sequences and compressing each into separate memory states.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a scalable alternative for long‑sequence language models, potentially improving performance and reducing resource demands.

items.summary: Diffusion language models offer a promising path to efficient agents through parallel token generation. However, efficient interaction requires adapting both where computation is spent and how much text is generated. items.summary: Language models pretrained on web corpora collected over multiple years learn both general and domain-specific knowledge. How these different kinds of knowledge are learned as pretraining progresses remains unclear. items.title: Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions
items.summary: When an LLM group's discussion is compressed into a short memory for a final decision maker, what should the memory keep? Two natural heuristics keep the rarest claims or the claims relevant to the decision criteria. On hidden-profile tasks both look attractive, because how widely a fact is held is confounded with whether it helps. We introduce CrossProfile, a diagnostic benchmark of 60 templates…

items.title: VideoLVR: Latent Visual Reasoning over Grounded Video Evidence
items.summary: Chain-of-thought reasoning has substantially advanced video understanding in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). However, language-based reasoning traces do not provide a reliable mechanism for models to revisit relevant visual evidence, leading to visual forgetting and impairing their ability to reason over video content. items.title: Beyond Answer Changes: Matched Same-Class Controls for Local Audio Evidence
items.summary: For audio-language models, an answer change after a local sound-event edit can reflect a response to the event's class, sensitivity to waveform rewriting, or both. We compare matched same-class and different-class replacements of a queried event. items.title: MoI-Bench: A Benchmark for Image Generation and Editing on Mobile Devices
items.summary: Developing on-device image models requires considering practical user needs, task types and device resource constraints. However, existing benchmarks provide limited guidance on identifying capability gaps between on-device models and server-side models. We introduce MoI-Bench, a benchmark grounded in mobile user needs, comprising 64 subtasks and 1150 samples. It defines 16 operations, such as…

items.title: GAS-PFN: Graph-Aware Spatiotemporal Prior-Data Fitted Networks for Zero-Shot Traffic Forecasting
items.summary: Traffic forecasting requires modeling complex temporal dynamics and the spatial dependencies imposed by road topology. Supervised graph-based models achieve strong performance, but are often trained for a particular dataset and sensor graph, making deployment to new or evolving networks costly.
